## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`refresh_fingerprints` must be fixed before merge: it overwrites the stored digest of any tracked file named in the call, so a hand-edited file passes `verify` after a refresh, contrary to the guarantee the description states. The refresh test also cannot detect the loss of unnamed manifest entries.

## Changes
Adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`, along with an unused `REVIEW_NOTE` string constant. Adds `tests/test_integrity.py` with one test per helper.

## Critical
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — refresh_fingerprints re-blesses hand-edited tracked files — Calling `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` after `tracked.txt` was hand-edited replaces its stored digest with the edited file's digest, so `verify` returns True. Line 17 assigns unconditionally, unlike the `if name not in entries` guard at line 24; the description says existing fingerprints detect hand edits. — A refresh after adding files silently erases the evidence of tampering in any tracked file named in the call. — Fix: Either skip names already in `entries` as `app/integrity.py:24` does, or, if re-fingerprinting is intended, say so in the description and pin it by editing `tracked.txt` in `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries`.

## Important
- tests/test_integrity.py:17 — tests — Assert manifest contents after the empty refresh — If `refresh_fingerprints` rebuilt the manifest from `names` alone, the call with `[]` would write `{}` and `verify` at line 18 would still return True, because `all()` over no entries is True. The call at line 12 names every entry, so it cannot catch the loss either. — A regression that drops unnamed entries, which disables verification for those files, would pass this test. — Fix: Compare the manifest to the expected dict after the empty call, as `tests/test_integrity.py:34` does.
